::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Use tikz (for example) to draw pictures in hyperbolic geometry](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/16617/use-tikz-for-example-to-draw-pictures-in-hyperbolic-geometry), asked by [John Palmieri](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/262/john-palmieri) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-04-25; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I would like to draw pictures in the [Poincaré disk model](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poincar%C3%A9_disk_model) for hyperbolic geometry.  Are there any built-in or add-on packages for tikz to do this?  For example, it would be nice to have functions for drawing [Saccheri quadrilaterals][q-1] or [Lambert quadrilaterals][q-2] or asymptotic triangles.
>
> (In my brief use so far, the [tkz-euclide](http://www.altermundus.fr/pages/euclide.html) package looks very good for Euclidean geometry, and now I'm looking for a hyperbolic analogue of it.)
>
>
>   [q-1]: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saccheri_quadrilateral
>   [q-2]: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambert_quadrilateral
:::

Probably not.  I googled "latex hyperbolic geometry" and the top hit was this page.  There are plenty of papers about hyperbolic geometry written in latex but no packages that I found for hyperbolic geometry. 

But I think these things can be done in TikZ, if one works hard enough.
